grandparents_cupboard.reason: Peaches, redcurrants, honey, butter, oats, almonds, cinnamon and Greek yoghurt are all plain whole foods.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including a punnet of redcurrants in July, is a normal Tesco buy at an everyday price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, a small bowl and a baking dish, and rubbing in is beginner technique.

works.reason: Four peach halves topped with currants, honey and an oat crumble at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes will soften and burst nicely for four.

honest_times.reason: Halving peaches, stripping currants, chopping almonds and rubbing in fits in 10 minutes, and 25 minutes of baking matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon are used, and nothing unlisted appears in the steps.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm fruit bake suits early July, and 150g of redcurrants bursting into the juices is a real part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, oats, nuts and yoghurt with only a little honey make a wholesome snack a family would happily eat again.
